clue.text: Reversing economies, school carried out decorative work

indicators.note: the clue opens by telling us to turn the next word round, so the economies are read backwards

parts.note: economies are cuts in spending
a coed is a coeducational school, taking both boys and girls

explanation.surface: A school, having reversed its cost-cutting, pays for some ornamental building work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversing' applies only to the economies word; a coed is a mixed school, a term more common in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: To stucco a wall is to coat it in decorative plaster, so plastering ornamentally is this past-tense verb.

clue.text: Blunt, perhaps, attribute shown by soldiers

parts.note: an attribute is a trait, a characteristic
OR, other ranks, stands for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Bluntness is a quality soldiers often display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blunt' looks like the adjective, but it is Anthony Blunt, the art historian exposed as a Soviet spy; 'perhaps' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Blunt spied for the Soviet Union, an example of someone betraying his country.

clue.text: Frank leader cutting attractive figure after endless fool

indicators.note: after places the trimmed magnet word behind the trimmed fool word
without its end, so the final letter of the word for a fool is dropped

parts.note: a charley (or charlie) is a fool

indicators.note: cutting here means docking the tail of the word for an attractive figure

parts.note: a magnet is a figure that attracts, literally or as a popular person

explanation.surface: A leader with frank manners cuts a charismatic figure after an incessant idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like an adjective but means one of the Franks, the Germanic people. 'endless' and 'cutting' each dock a final letter; charley is a variant spelling of charlie, a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlemagne was King of the Franks and later the first Holy Roman Emperor.

clue.text: Tender king, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly tells us the word for a king is to be heard rather than written

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famous for Offa's Dyke

explanation.surface: A kindly monarch, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like the adjective 'gentle' but is the verb or noun for a proposal; OFFA, the Anglo-Saxon king, sounds like it in a non-rhotic British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender is to present a proposal or bid, the same as to make a bid.

clue.text: Abandon court rule? Small amount of liquid shown

parts.note: to drop something is to abandon it
a let is a tennis court ruling that a point be replayed

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a legal regulation be scrapped, with a little liquid on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court; it is the tennis court, where a let is called.
explanation.definitionFit: A droplet is a tiny drop, a very small quantity of fluid.

clue.text: Actress with a lot of competition facing dismissal

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, so the last letter of the competition word goes

parts.note: a cup is a competition, like the FA Cup
the dismissal word comes after, facing the trimmed competition word

explanation.surface: An actress in a fiercely competitive field is about to be fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinéad, Joan and John Cusack are all screen performers sharing this surname.

clue.text: Mexican man's best friend?

parts.note: the dog is man's best friend, and the tiny breed named after a Mexican state is the obvious Mexican one

explanation.definitionFit: This tiny dog breed is named after a state of Mexico, and dogs are called man's best friend.

clue.text: Place for recovering suit (not half!)

indicators.note: not half means only part of the card suit is kept, its back three letters dropped

parts.note: spades is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Somewhere to recover a suit, and not just half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half!' is British slang for 'absolutely', disguising the instruction to drop half of SPADES.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a resort with healing waters where people go to recuperate.

clue.text: Retired priest featured in very fashionable channel

indicators.note: featured in places the reversed priest inside the fashionable word

parts.note: cult as an adjective means hugely popular with a devoted following

indicators.note: retired means going backwards, so the priest's title is reversed

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A clergyman who has stepped down appears on a trendy TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' reverses the priest's title, and 'featured in' sets it inside the word for very fashionable; 'channel' is a watercourse, not TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A culvert is a drain or tunnel carrying water under a road, so a watercourse.

clue.text: Unusually warm foal? It lay in a remote place

indicators.note: unusually signals that the following letters appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A foal is oddly warm; it is lying out in the wilds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges WARM FOAL IT LAY into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being far from everyday life and crowds means being somewhere isolated.

clue.text: Second old coin is more out-of-date

parts.note: the taler or thaler was an old German silver coin

explanation.surface: Another antique coin is even more dated.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'more out-of-date'; 'is' joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale things are past their best, so the comparative means further past freshness.

clue.text: Boat turning on missile installation?

parts.note: a launch is a motorboat

indicators.note: turning reverses the short word for on

parts.note: re means on, as in 'on the subject of'

explanation.surface: A boat turning towards a missile site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A launcher is a device that fires rockets, so a missile installation; the question mark marks the loose fit.

clue.text: Cameron's lot set about opening of this network — causing spat?

indicators.note: set about places these MPs round the letters that follow

parts.note: David Cameron led the Conservatives, so his lot are Con MPs

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a rete is a network of nerves or blood vessels

explanation.surface: The Conservative party attacks the launch of a broadcasting network, which sparks a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' wraps Cameron's Conservative MPs round the first letter of 'this' plus the network; 'spat' is a quarrel, not the past of spit.
explanation.definitionFit: A contretemps is a minor disagreement or squabble.

clue.text: Group pocketing international money provoked chat in TV programme

indicators.note: pocketing means the crew holds the abbreviations inside it

parts.note: a crew is a group of people working together

indicators.note: provoked means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A gang pocketing foreign cash sparked a conversation on a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketing' puts the two abbreviations inside the group, and 'provoked' stirs the chat letters, which follow. Crimewatch was a long-running BBC show appealing for help with unsolved crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimewatch was a BBC television series reconstructing crimes to appeal for witnesses.

clue.text: One using an automatic communications facility?

definitions.text: One using an automatic communications facility?

parts.words: One using an automatic communications facility?
parts.note: facility means skill: the clue describes someone whose skill with language comes as if automatically, while pretending to describe a machine user

explanation.definitionFit: A wordsmith is a skilled writer, someone with a natural facility for language.

clue.text: Observe night in Rome devoid of heart?

indicators.note: devoid of heart means one of the central letters of the Italian word is taken away

parts.note: notte is Italian for night

explanation.surface: Watching a Roman night without much feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing one of the two middle Ts of NOTTE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to notice or take heed of it.

clue.text: Horse getting to weaken around start of course

indicators.note: around places the sagging word outside the first letter of the next word

parts.note: to sag is to droop or weaken

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A racehorse starts to tire at the beginning of the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is slang for heroin, as is the answer, so the racing picture misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang names for heroin.

clue.text: Soup? Food put with wine on reflection

parts.note: chow is slang for food

indicators.note: on reflection means seen as in a mirror, so the wine is read backwards

parts.note: red is red wine

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, soup is the food to serve with the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns RED into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup, typically of seafood.

clue.text: Grill might feature in this building near a trust

indicators.note: building means constructing, so these letters are assembled into something new

explanation.surface: A building next to a trust could include a grill.
explanation.walkthrough: Grill here is a restaurant name, as in 'The Savoy Grill', while 'building' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Many restaurants include 'Grill' in their names, or cook on a grill.

clue.text: School item kept by girls at Cheltenham

indicators.note: kept by signals letters held within the next few words, running across them

explanation.surface: Something for school owned by pupils at Cheltenham Ladies' College.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'girlS AT CHELtenham'. Cheltenham is an English town with famous schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag for carrying books to school.

clue.text: Representative offered prospect in revolutionary age

indicators.note: in places the prospect word inside the reversed age
revolutionary means turned round, so the age is read backwards

parts.note: an eon is an age
to prospect is to search for minerals, as a mine does

explanation.surface: A delegate offered a vision during an age of revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses the age, and 'in' places the prospect word inside it; 'offered' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone put forward to act or stand for others.

clue.text: Season, we hear, linked to some tennis in county

indicators.note: we hear means the season's name is listened to rather than spelt

parts.note: summer is a season
a set is a portion of a tennis match

explanation.surface: Summer, they say, is linked with a bit of tennis in the county.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMERSET is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is an English county in the south-west.

clue.text: Inter Milan's No 1? Outside bet no foul is seen

indicators.note: outside means the anagrammed letters wrap round the first letter of the Italian city
foul means corrupt, so these letters are mixed up
number one is the first letter

explanation.surface: An Inter Milan match where betting irregularities are suspected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inter' looks like the Milan football club but is the verb 'bury'. 'foul' scrambles the bet letters, which go 'Outside' Milan's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter a body is to bury it, placing it in a tomb.

clue.text: Diminutive fellow accepted by upstanding banker

indicators.note: accepted by means the fellow is taken into the reversed river
in a down clue, upstanding means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a banker is a river, something with banks; here the Nile

explanation.surface: A small man is taken on by an upright bank employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' means a river, here the NILE, reversed to ELIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small and delicate, like an elf.

clue.text: Fuss in house beginning to mount amid return of inferior actor

parts.note: a dust, or dust-up, is a fuss or commotion

indicators.note: amid places the first letter of the mount word inside the reversed slang word
return of means the word for inferior is read backwards

parts.note: naff is British slang for poor quality or tacky

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Commotion at home as a poor actor begins to climb back.
explanation.walkthrough: NAFF reversed gives FFAN, with M (start of 'mount') inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dustin Hoffman is the American star of The Graduate and Rain Man.

clue.text: Rag students set up

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word is reversed, reading upward

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: Students produce a rag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rag' looks like a student charity rag but means a downmarket newspaper; The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, and a rag is a disparaging word for such a paper.

clue.text: Staff giving up time for new crisis

indicators.note: giving up means a letter is surrendered, with another put in its place

parts.note: a crutch is a staff to lean on

explanation.surface: Staff giving up time for a fresh emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees but is a walking aid, CRUTCH; its T is swapped for N.
explanation.definitionFit: A crunch is a critical moment or decisive point.

clue.text: Artist having to win backing of Welshman?

parts.note: to land something is to win it

indicators.note: backing of means the Welsh name is reversed

parts.note: Rees is a common Welsh name

explanation.surface: An artist hoping to gain the support of someone from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing of' turns REES into SEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter, known for animal paintings and the Trafalgar Square lions.
